question: A 16-year-old boy presents to the emergency department after a skateboarding accident. He fell on a broken bottle and received a 4 cm wound on the dorsal aspect of his left hand. His vitals are stable and he was evaluated by the surgeon on call who determined to suture was not required. After several weeks the wound has almost completely healed (see image). Which of the following is the correct description of this patient’s wound before healing?
analysis: The description of the wound as resulting from falling on a broken bottle and being 4 cm in size on the dorsal aspect of the hand suggests it is a laceration. Lacerations are irregular tears in the skin caused by a blunt trauma, which in this case is likely due to the impact and tearing effect of the broken glass. Incised wounds are clean cuts by sharp objects, which does not align with the 'broken bottle' scenario as perfectly as a laceration does. Abrasions involve superficial damage and are more about scraping. Avulsions involve tearing away of a body structure or part, and punctures are deep, narrow wounds like a stab, which does not fit the description of a 4 cm surface wound.
